page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is a big data and storage-focused virtual machine instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor offering 6 physical cores and 12 vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture. The system is provisioned with 48.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes a 4 Gbps baseline network interface. An outstanding physical attribute is its bundled 35,433 GB local HDD storage array, designed for data-intensive storage workloads without requiring external block volumes.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture oriented toward multi-threaded throughput over single-threaded burst capability. Single-core performance falls into lower tiers, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 911.0 and a single-core stress-ng result of 1102.49. However, aggregate processing scales stably under parallel execution, delivering a Geekbench multi-core score of 4584.0, a PassMark CPU score of 10074.03, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 37.67 GB/sec. Memory subsystem testing reflects 54.9 GB/sec read and 47.08 GB/sec write bandwidth on large un-cached blocks.

The primary architectural tradeoff is the reliance on mechanical HDD storage alongside an older Intel Xeon microarchitecture. While random I/O and single-thread execution speeds are modest, the provision of over 35 TB of attached physical disk space per instance delivers high storage density. This hardware configuration is suited for batch processing, large-scale data ingestion, log archives, distributed Hadoop or MapReduce clusters, and cold or warm analytical data lakes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.3xlarge is a big data instance running on a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor with 12 dedicated vCPUs, 6 physical cores, and 48.0 GB of memory. Designed primarily for massive localized capacity, it features 35,433 GB of integrated local HDD storage and a 4 Gbps baseline network allocation. Performance benchmarks demonstrate modest single-thread capabilities, recording a 911.0 Geekbench single-core score, but moderate parallel throughput with a PassMark CPU score of 10074.03 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression of 37.67 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth reaches 54.9 GB/sec on sequential large-block reads. Lacking hardware GPU accelerators, the instance trades high-speed solid-state random I/O for exceptional raw spinning-disk storage density. This makes it an appropriate platform for big data batch pipelines, distributed file storage clusters such as HDFS, and sequential log analytics.
